messages:
ada: Heads-up — in eu-west3 I'm seeing a cluster of GPU nodes fail provisioning with local volume checksum mismatches after the overlayfs kernel module update rolled last night.

miles: repro steps? happened during normal batch launches?

ada: yes, during large-batch launches. Provisioner tries to attach scratch, node boots containers, then some jobs hit read errors from /scratch, kube evicts and we get provisioning timeouts.

kai: logs? any dmesg/blk errors?

ada: pasted a snippet from one affected host:
```
[  123.456789] overlayfs: warning: dentry xattr mismatch on /scratch/stripe_map
[  123.456803] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 204800
[  123.456811] local-disk-manager: scrub failed: checksum_mismatch stripe_map id=0x4f2a
```

lucy: stripe_map mismatch — is this the janitor/cleaner touching metadata concurrently with kernel overlayfs relinks?

ada: that's our suspicion. The new overlayfs path-handling is slightly different w.r.t. publish/unpublish ordering, which looks like it can expose a window where the cleaner updates metadata while kernel returns stale dentry lookups.

jen: any correlation with scrub schedule? which cleaner epoch?

ada: looks like scrub runs every 10m by default; the failures cluster right after a large batch churn where many ephemeral volumes are created+destroyed.

miles: could be a TOCTOU between binder unmount and metadata flush. We saw similar staleness during the fstrim scheduler spike months ago but not this exact codepath.

ops-scheduler: deploy-bot scheduled overlayfs/driver upgrade canary to eu-west3 at 02:00 UTC yesterday (rollout 20% -> 100%).

jen: ops-scheduler — can we rollback the module? or at least pause rollout?

ops-scheduler: paused rollout at 02:12 UTC after first alerts. Remaining nodes still on old module.

miles: mitigation idea: short-term force-local-cleaner to hold per-volume metadata locks during rename/unlink. Locking will increase scrub latency but reduce races.

ada: we pushed a hotfix to the cleaner to add a cheap O(1) rename lock on the directory — rolled to a subset, helped one host recover.

kai: what's the real impact? number of failed launches and cost?

ada: ~18 provisioning failures in eu-west3 over 2 hours, 12 job retries, roughly 45 GPU-minutes lost. Not huge but it's causing customer-facing retries.

lucy: we should also add a defensive check in the serving runtime: on checksum_mismatch treat as transient and proactively re-attach backend from a different scratch pool before failing request. Lower latency but avoids cascading evictions.

jen: agree. fallback to network-backed scratch (slower) would keep jobs running. Needs knob in provisioning policy.

miles: short-term runbook: 1) pause overlayfs rollout (done), 2) pin new allocations to old kernel nodes for 2h (scheduling rule), 3) hotfix cleaner rename lock (deploy to canary), 4) add transient reattach fallback in provisioner.

ada: implemented scheduling rule: annotate node pools eu-west3-oldkernel and set admission control to prefer them for 2h.

ops-scheduler: annotation applied at 15:06 UTC. New allocations should avoid canary nodes.

sre-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-0454 "overlayfs dentry race causing stripe_map checksum_mismatch in eu-west3" assigned to eng-infra.

miles: long-term we need to: a) upstream kernel report & patch (overlayfs publish ordering), b) cleaner redesign to persist atomic metadata updates, c) add metric for stripe_map staleness and a gauge for rename-contention.

kai: can we instrument the cleaner to emit a small histogram: time between unlink and metadata-flush, and counter for rename-retries?

ada: yes — pushing small metrics PR now.

lucy: also run targeted scrub sweep across eu-west3 scratchpool with lower concurrency to heal any corrupted stripe_map entries. We'll throttle to avoid iops spikes.

jen: what's the risk of extra scrubs on wear? local SSD write cycles are finite — we need to balance healing vs wear. Ops: run at 10% concurrency with wear-aware scheduler.

miles: cost note: extra scrubs ~ 300GB write per hour at 10% concurrency, estimated wear impact <0.05% per disk lifecycle. Acceptable for safety window.

ada: hotfix rollout status: cleaner-lock rolled to 6 canary nodes at 15:40 UTC, no new checksum_mismatch on those. Rolling to 30% now.

ops-scheduler: deploy-bot: rolling update to cleaner-hotfix started (30% -> 100%) trigger at 15:45 UTC.

jen: schedule a kernel regression bisect with vendor — assign to miles + kai.

miles: taking vendor lane, will open bug with kernel tree and attach repro kernel logs + minimal repro.

kai: creating probe job that reproduces TOCTOU locally — will share artifact link.

ada: immediate customer-facing mitigation: set provisioning fallback to network-scratch for eu-west3 for 3h — config uploaded.

lucy: re-run failed jobs? we requeued them automatically; most resumed once pinned to oldkernel nodes.

miles: next steps and owners: (1) miles/kai -> kernel bug + repro (2) ada -> metric PR + provisioning fallback knob (3) lucy -> scrub sweep plan + wear throttle (4) jen -> postmortem template and SLA impact calc.

ada: small note — we should add a synthetic test that does rapid create/delete of ephemeral volumes with overlayfs to catch regressions in CI. Filing ticket now.

jen: thanks all. I'll start postmortem draft and link incident. If we see any resurgence revert rollout immediately. :thumbsup:

ada: updated status 16:20 UTC: cleaner-hotfix at 100% in eu-west3, provisioning fallback enabled, scrub sweep at 10% concurrency. No new failures in last 20m.

miles: will keep kernel bug open until upstream confirms patch. Closing temporary scheduling pin after 3h unless anomalies reappear.

sre-bot: INC-2026-0454 status -> mitigated.

ada: closing thread for now, will add postmortem link when jen posts it.
